text: Recognizing illness (ការសង្កេតសញ្ញាជំងឺ) across cattle, pigs, and poultry starts with knowing what's normal for each animal and checking regularly rather than waiting for severe illness. Observe appetite, water consumption, movement, breathing, behavior, body condition, manure/droppings, and production (eggs, milk, growth). Warning signs: separating from the group, weakness, unusual aggression or depression, difficulty standing/walking, coughing, sneezing, discharge, rapid or difficult breathing, diarrhea, vomiting, abnormal droppings, skin lesions, weight loss, reproductive problems, or an unexpected production drop. These are warning signs, NOT diagnoses -- many diseases overlap in symptoms, and heat stress, poor nutrition, toxins, injury, or poor housing can look similar. During the wet season, watch wet/muddy housing, contaminated water, and parasites; during the dry season, heat stress, dehydration, and reduced feed can also produce disease-like signs. For poultry, flock-level changes (many birds suddenly eating less, inactive, or laying fewer eggs) are often more informative than one bird's symptoms. A simple notebook is enough: record date, animal type, number affected, key signs, deaths, recent purchases/movements, feed changes, vaccination info, and unusual weather. Seek veterinary help urgently for sudden unexplained mortality, rapidly increasing sick animals, severe breathing difficulty, widespread neurological signs, severe diarrhea in many animals, hemorrhagic signs, or multiple abortions. Never collapse an observation straight into a diagnosis -- distinguish what the farmer observed, general knowledge about possible causes, and an actual professional diagnosis.
